title: Impact flashes
purpose: Teach that meteoroids hitting the Moon make brief flashes, how NASA watches for them, and why two telescopes must agree.

beats.label: diagram
beats.credit: NASA's rule: two telescopes must agree

beats.label: measured
beats.sub: The chapter's flash candidates are written for the game

captions: Tiny bits of space rock hit the Moon and make brief flashes of light.
NASA watches the Moon's dark side for them about {nights} nights a month.
In the first five years they confirmed {count} flashes, {pct} during meteor showers.
A camera can glitch, so one sighting is not enough.
A flash counts only when two telescopes both see it at the same moment.
These flashes were watched from Earth.
ends_on: Trust a reading when two independent checks agree, not when one says so.
